Quick Dollar Drawdown Estimator (2000–2025 Historical Data)

Crossing the $1,000,000 retirement milestone changes the psychological weight of daily volatility. A routine 10% correction equals $100,000, and a full bear market can temporarily wipe out half a million dollars if equity exposure sits unbuffered.

In our 2000–2025 historical tables, a $1M saver allocating 15% ($150,000) to short-term Treasury liquidity (SGOV) holds nearly four full years of $40,000 annual draws outside equity market swings. That time runway removes the urge to capitulate during extreme fear regimes.

Why does $150,000 in SGOV matter so much on a $1M portfolio?

At $40,000 in annual portfolio withdrawals, $150,000 covers 45 months of living expenses without selling a single depressed share of SMH or XLV during a downturn.
